title: Function, not biography: the Paul function and the Johannine aperture function
description: Historical theses from the Revelation First work plans (#1400, #832, June 2026) and staging document (#847) argue that named scriptural figures are author-functions rather than biographical individuals: Paul as the adversarial probe a heteronymic mystery system generates against its own indeterminacy, and the Baptist, Evangelist, Elder and Revelator as positions within one Johannine aperture-function. The Feist Source (#852) argues the same of the Logos, resolved by its archive into the biography of Jesus, and the Capture Registry (#3) reads an AI Overview card as carrying the Paul function at its sharpest. The page also holds unrelated claims on the strawberry diagnostic and on operative feminism.

claims.statement: The Baptist and the Revelator collapse into a single aperture-function -- **the Johannine Aperture Function.** Not "the same biographical man" but a structural unity that historical-individual frameworks cannot parse. The tradition's unsolved "which John?" problem is the fingerprint of the heteronymic architecture showing through the conventional framework. The better formulation: the Baptist, the Evangelist, the Elder, and the Revelator are not rival historical candidates. They are differentiated positions within a Johannine aperture-function: witness, vision, theological elaboration, and governance.

claims.statement: In the Johannine archive: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." The Logos is the operative creative principle — the function that makes meaning possible. The function became incarnate. The archive received the incarnation and resolved it into a biography: Jesus of Nazareth, born in Bethlehem under Augustus, crucified under Pontius Pilate. The resolution generated the canonical tradition. The tradition cannot recover the function because its own existence depends on the biographical resolution.

claims.registered_title: The Second Crucifixion: Power, Sorcery, and the Inversion of the Operative Word (EA-REVFIRST-CRUCIFIXION-01)
claims.statement: **The structural diagnosis:** Rabbinic tradition preserves a structural memory in which the disputed power is not dismissed as mere fraud but treated as dangerous operative practice. *Kishuf* is the charge reserved for real operative practice, not for stage magic. *Mesit* is the charge reserved for someone whose words actually move people, not for someone whose words fail. The Talmudic tradition does not deny the operative word. It condemns its deployment — a distinction that only makes sense if the power was experienced as real.
